Inconsistencies in basic biographical facts that don't add up when compared across different conversations.

approved_draft.why_this_matters: A record accumulates that the person has no opportunity to answer as it is built, and by the time they see it, it reads as damning.
approved_draft.what_it_is_not: Standard documentation applied to everyone is not targeting. A genuine record of concerns that were actually raised with the person is legitimate even if they wish it did not exist. Someone keeping notes on their own experience for their own reference is doing something ordinary.

existing_specific_text.short_definition: Creating false or misleading documentation designed to build a case against the target, often without their knowledge.
existing_specific_text.expanded_definition: Creating false or misleading documentation — emails, notes, formal write-ups — specifically designed to build a case against the target over time, often without the target's knowledge that a case is even being built. Unlike a single False Report, this is a sustained, patient process: individual pieces of documentation accumulate into a record that looks damning in aggregate, even if each piece alone seems minor.
existing_specific_text.plain_language_summary: In plain terms: creating false or misleading documentation designed to build a case against the target, often without their knowledge.
existing_specific_text.why_this_matters: Patterns like this can shape communication, trust, and decision-making — left unnamed, they can contribute to misplaced trust in a distorted picture of a situation, discovered later, if at all. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.
what_it_is: Creating false or misleading documentation designed to build a case against the target, often without their knowledge.
what_it_sounds_like: Formal write-ups or documented "concerns" about the target that don't match the target's own understanding of the events described.
The target discovers, much later, an extensive paper trail being built about them that they were never made aware of at the time.
Documentation that seems oddly detailed or one-sided, as though written with an eventual audience in mind.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Standard documentation practices in workplaces and institutions exist for legitimate reasons and apply broadly. Keeping a personal record of real events for one's own reference isn't inherently building a case against someone.
common_false_positives: Legitimate, standard documentation practices that apply to everyone, not specifically targeted at one person.
A genuine record of real, previously-discussed concerns, even if the target wishes it hadn't been documented.
Someone documenting their own experience for their own reference, without any intent to build a case.
discernment_questions: Does the documentation accurately reflect events, or does it selectively frame things unfavorably?
Is documentation applied evenly to everyone in the relevant context, or specifically concentrated on the target?
Was the target aware that documentation was happening and given a chance to share their own account?
Does the volume and detail of documentation seem disproportionate to any legitimate purpose?
less_concerning_if: Documentation is accurate, applied evenly, and the target has been aware of and able to respond to it.
more_concerning_if: Documentation is one-sided, concentrated specifically on the target, and built without their knowledge.
existing_specific_text.repair_check: After the incident, was there a genuine acknowledgment (not a non-apology), a concrete change in behavior, and no repeat of the same pattern? Repair is a pattern of change over time, not a single sentence of regret.
existing_specific_text.boundary_respect_check: When a boundary was stated plainly in this area, was it honored going forward — or tested, ignored, punished, or reframed as unreasonable? Boundary respect observed over multiple instances is one of the more reliable signals available.
existing_specific_text.psychological_mechanism: One documented mechanism behind patterns like this is that they can operate by controlling what information the other person has access to, so their conclusions are built on an incomplete or false picture. This describes a possible mechanism, not a claim about what any specific person intended.
existing_specific_text.possible_impact_on_receiver: People sometimes describe misplaced trust in a distorted picture of a situation, discovered later, if at all in connection with patterns like this. Impact varies widely by person, history, and context — this is a possibility to consider, not a predicted or universal outcome, and it is not a diagnosis of the person on the receiving end of a sustained pattern like this.
existing_specific_text.safety_note: No elevated safety concern is implied by this entry on its own. If a situation ever does involve threats, monitoring, isolation, or fear for your safety, the general guidance still applies: A phrase-matching tool cannot decide safety. If this involves threats, monitoring, isolation, sex, money, housing, immigration, self-harm pressure, retaliation, or fear for safety, prioritize real-world support from a trusted person, local support service, legal/workplace resource, or emergency help if immediate danger exists.
misuse_warning: One example is a signal to examine, not proof of motive, diagnosis, abuse, danger, or character. Do not use this label to attack, shame, threaten, expose, or retaliate against someone.

approved_draft.why_this_matters: No single person can see enough to raise a question, so accountability fails not because anyone refused it but because nobody had the view required to ask for it.
approved_draft.what_it_is_not: Confidentiality and need-to-know structures exist for genuinely good reasons in most organisations. Information silos form naturally in any large family or workplace. Someone who simply did not think to pass something on has partitioned nothing.

existing_specific_text.short_definition: Structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
existing_specific_text.expanded_definition: Structuring information — in a family, workplace, or organization — so that no single person has access to the full picture, which has the effect of limiting anyone's ability to hold the person controlling the information accountable, since no one else can see enough to connect the dots. Each individual piece of information may be shared honestly; the deception lives in how the pieces are kept apart.
existing_specific_text.plain_language_summary: In plain terms: structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
existing_specific_text.why_this_matters: Patterns like this can shape communication, trust, and decision-making — left unnamed, they can contribute to misplaced trust in a distorted picture of a situation, discovered later, if at all. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.
what_it_is: Structuring information so no one person can see the full picture, limiting accountability and oversight.
what_it_sounds_like: Different people in the same family or organization each have a different, partial understanding of the same situation.
Questions that would require connecting information from multiple sources get deflected or discouraged.
The full picture only becomes visible when, by chance, two people who each have partial information happen to compare notes.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Legitimate confidentiality and natural information silos exist in most families and organizations without any intent to avoid accountability. Not proactively sharing everything with everyone isn't automatically a control tactic.
common_false_positives: Legitimate confidentiality or need-to-know structures that exist for genuinely appropriate reasons.
Natural information silos that develop in any large family or organization without deliberate intent to prevent accountability.
A person simply not thinking to share information broadly, rather than deliberately withholding it from specific people.
discernment_questions: Is there a legitimate reason for the information to be compartmentalized, or does it seem to specifically prevent accountability?
Does connecting the compartmentalized pieces reveal something the person controlling the information wouldn't want revealed?
Are people actively discouraged from comparing notes, or does that discouragement just happen not to occur?
Would this person be uncomfortable if the full picture were assembled and shared openly?
less_concerning_if: Any compartmentalization has a legitimate, non-accountability-avoiding reason.
more_concerning_if: The compartmentalization specifically prevents anyone from seeing a pattern that would otherwise be concerning, and connecting information is discouraged.
